A3_S6_D1: ^Panther: If you plan on foraging tomorrow…
^Carti: Would you like to go together?
^Panther: With how the rain and wind has shaken the trees, I worry you forest watchers would slip whilst climbing branches.
^Carti: In that case… I suppose we’ll be searching for eggs and fruits tomorrow. Things up on the trees.
^Carti: I’m sure not all of us would slip, though.
^Carti: Remember when she won that game of tag?
^Panther: I didn’t think an omnivore could be so silent.
A3_S6_D2: ^Aspho: I haven’t seen those tapestries in a while. Looks like Oren’s relationship with the humans is good as ever?
^Faile: Remember the first time he tried to request borrowing them?
^Faile: We were all still kids at the time…
^Aspho: Including their now-head craftsman, with a tongue sharper than any of ours combined!
^Aspho: Ah… it’s a wonder that Oren managed to win them over in the end.
^Narrator: The two nod, telling you and Amelia about how Oren spent three days and three nights over at the human settlement, demonstrating his style of storytelling until they were convinced.
^Faile: To be fair, those tapestries are historical records. I wouldn’t want to hand it off to just anyone, either.
^Aspho: And now, Oren is pretty popular every time he visits their village. Usually to return tapestries and borrow new ones, much to that sharp-tongued lad’s chargrain.
A3_S6_D3: ^Calf: It’s you! These are the people who saved me, Mom!
^Anana: Thank you so much, you two. Did Chione pass on the jewelry as thanks?
^Noelle: Yes, it’s with me right now.
^Narrator: The monsteratops nods. From her kind tone, you can imagine that she smiled.
^Anana: These items are symbolic of our history on the island, and actions our ancestors took to protect this land.
^Anana: We have many stories of our own, which are told to the Viridi when they are young.
^Amelia: My ‘gran used to tell me that your kind were fierce warriors.
^Anana: Haha, perhaps back in the day — when predators and prey were still fighting over land.
^Anana: Our strength and size are gifts, so that we may protect what matters most.
^Anana: These days, such ‘protection’ is extended to the Viridi, along with any who identify themselves as Thavma.
^Noelle: I’ve noticed that the people here aren’t really concerned with species.
^Calf: It’s better that way, isn’t it?
^Calf: Birds can help us find items when they’re lost, while we can let them roost on our backs.
^Calf: …Last night, I was meaning to find something I buried nearby the ruins, to give to Oren. I thought it’d inspire a fun story.
^Calf: But everything looks the same at night… and I got stuck inside instead.
^Noelle: Some beetles noticed your trail in the ruins’ way, and a panther heard your cries.
^Amelia: “The forest remembers all who passed and still live within.”
^Anana: Maybe you should tell Oren about your adventure.
^Anana: He’s very good at spinning tales, after all.
A3_S6_D4: ^Elder: Ah… It feels monumental for me to be alive during one of the Great Floods.
^Elder: Are your preparations to move into the mountains underway?
^Amaya: We’re keeping an eye on the weather. So long as the floods stay on schedule, we still have time.
^Chione: I’ll send you our stock-checks soon! A lot of the herbs we have are still undergoing preservation. But it should be enough for a month or two in the caves.
^Oren: I’ve been looking through our old records. Other than the usual supplies… I think it’d also be worth transporting entertainment items, if we have the time.
^Oren: Cabin fever begins around the second week. Oh! And there were issues regarding the lack of sunlight.
^Chione: Some plants that glow in the dark should help if we create a ‘daylight zone’ in the caves. And it should burn less fuel for lamps and such.
^Amaya: …Once, I ran into a Krakenfolk who was traveling in the night. And when he jumped, thinking I was an attacker — his hair glowed bright, like the plankton that affects the waves.
^Amaya: I’m sure they can’t do it for hours on end, but it may be worth checking if any Krakenfolk are interested in becoming a sort of patrol unit.
^Amaya: Their ability to melt the darkness may prove useful in times like this.
